paper_metadata.title: Strengthening evaluation and high-temperature behavior of Ti–Fe–O–Cu–Si alloy

evidence.quote: Fully dense powder metallurgy (PM) Ti – 4Fe – 0.2O – 3Cu – 0.4Si alloy was produced employing spark plasma sin - tering (SPS) and hot extrusion aiming to develop an inexpensive high strength dual-phase ( α + β ) Ti alloy.

were used to fabricate Ti – 4Fe – 0.2O – 3Cu – (0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6) Si alloys by employing SPS system (heating rate: 20 ◦ C/min, sintering temperature: 1000 ◦ C and holding time: 60 min under 30 MPa uniaxial pressure).

The sintered specimens with 42 mm dia, 30 mm height were hot extruded to 10 mm rods by pre-heating at 850 ◦ C for 5 min using a 200-ton hydraulic press machine (SHP-200-450, Shibayama Kikai, Japan) with an extrusion speed of 6 mm/min.
The high-temperature tensile test samples first annealed at 500 ◦ C for 24 h and tested using a hori - zontal high-temperature tensile testing machine (CATY-T3H, YONE - KURA MFG).

Room temperature EBSD analysis revealed that the alloy consisted of globular (equiaxed) microstructure with a higher fraction of α phase (60 vol%) with a strong texture of < 10 10 > //extrusion direction
In contrast, β phase constitutes 40 vol% and < 101 > crystallographic texture.
Room temperature EBSD analysis revealed that the alloy consisted of globular (equiaxed) microstructure with a higher fraction of α phase (60 vol%)
having the sharp texture of < 10 10 > //extrusion direction
the fraction of high angle grain boundaries (87%) much higher than low angle grain boundaries which trigger feasible plastic deformation
Dual-phase Ti has α / β phase boundaries where sliding resistance is lower than α / α and β / β phase boundaries.
at 700 ◦ C α + β phase almost completely transformed to α phase and it remains stable until 900 ◦ C where α → β + α phase transformation occurs.
it remains stable until 900 ◦ C where α → β + α phase transformation occurs.

The microstructure observation at 700 ◦ C shows the grain coarsening about 35% and by increasing the temperature to 800 ◦ C average grain size increased slightly and reached 5.42 μ m (about 50% increase).
When the temperature raised to 900 ◦ C average grain size radically increased to 9.5 μ m.
Ti – 4Fe – 0.2O – 3Cu exhibited the yield strength of 987 MPa
the yield strength increased to 1075 MPa at 0.6% Si addition
The yielding occurred at ~370 MPa (more or less similar to Ti – 6Al – 4V in previous reports [ 16 , 17 ]) followed by strain-softening and high elongation more than 55% fracture strain.
followed by strain-softening and high elongation more than 55% fracture strain
The solid solution strengthening associated with Fe, Cu, and Si alloying elements calculated by Gypen – Toda model is 331 MPa.
As a well-known mechanism, the contribution of grain refinement to the strengthening can be calculated using Hall-Petch relationship
These observations imply that grain boundary mobility is restricted at ≤ 700 ◦ C due to the solute drag effect which impedes the grain growth.

According to Kitashima et al. [ 18 ], the interaction between Si atoms and dislocations gives rise to the energy barriers for slip and cross-slip which consequently triggers the strength improvement that can be sustained at high-temperatures.
it is assumed that α phase grains obstruct the dislocation motion, and the accumulation of dislocations generate a strain gradient at α / β interfaces and within the β matrix
